title: Measles transmission-related epidemiological parameter estimates: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

analysis.scope_and_question: This systematic review aims to provide a comprehensive resource of measles transmission-related epidemiological parameters.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: English and French primary studies of transmission-related epidemiological parameters were included, and standard systematic review methodology was followed.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Measles was characterized by a pooled incubation period (13.5 days, 95%CI 12.6–14.4; I2 = 95.9%), serial interval (12.4 days, 95%CI 11.5–13.4; I2 = 97.6%), symptom onset to hospitalization (4.8 days, 95%CI 3.7–5.8, I2 = 99.7%), and basic reproduction number median 11.5 (range of 0–57).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Subgroup analyses by World Health Organization (WHO) region, population, decade, and quality of reporting were conducted to explore heterogeneity.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: This work is part of a global epidemic preparedness and response project to establish an accessible living Global Repository of Epidemiological Parameters aimed at reducing duplicative efforts in identifying and summarizing epidemiological parameters.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review aims to provide a comprehensive resource of measles transmission-related epidemiological parameters. English and French primary studies of transmission-related epidemiological parameters were included, and standard systematic review methodology was followed. Measles was characterized by a pooled incubation period (13.5 days, 95%CI 12.6–14.4; I2 = 95.9%), serial interval (12.4 days, 95%CI 11.5–13.4; I2 = 97.6%), symptom onset to hospitalization (4.8 days, 95%CI 3.7–5.8, I2 = 99.7%), and basic reproduction number median 11.5 (range of 0–57). Subgroup analyses by World Health Organization (WHO) region, population, decade, and quality of reporting were conducted to explore heterogeneity. This work is part of a global epidemic preparedness and response project to establish an accessible living Global Repository of Epidemiological Parameters aimed at reducing duplicative efforts in identifying and summarizing epidemiological parameters.

title: Impact of a large measles outbreak associated with transmission in the Americas and Canada's loss of measles elimination status: descriptive cohort study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to describe the epidemiological characteristics, public health response, and evidence of international spread of a large measles outbreak that contributed to the loss of Canada’s measles elimination status.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a descriptive cohort analysis of measles outbreak cases reported to Ontario’s public health surveillance system during the outbreak period, which spanned epidemiological weeks 28 October 2024 to 6 October 2025. Participants included individuals meeting the outbreak case definition for confirmed or probable measles infection during this time.
analysis.methods: Cases were identified using an outbreak-specific case definition that incorporated epidemiological, clinical, laboratory, and viral sequencing criteria. Phylogenetic analysis of measles virus sequences was used to assess evidence of onwards spread to other countries.
analysis.main_results: The outbreak consisted of 2377 cases (2064 confirmed and 313 probable) over 49 weeks and contributed to the loss of Canada’s measles elimination status. Most cases (2146/2377, 90.3%) occurred among members of historically under-vaccinated communities, with limited spillover into the broader population.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as highlighting the risk of measles re-establishment in countries that have attained elimination and underscored the importance of culturally appropriate community engagement to build trust in immunisation and prevent future outbreaks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health strategies for measles surveillance, prevention, and community engagement to maintain elimination status and address immunity gaps in interconnected populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is descriptive in nature, and while it provides detailed epidemiological data, it does not include statistical analyses or causal conclusions. The evidence is strong for describing the outbreak characteristics and international spread.

analysis.summary_en: This study describes a large measles outbreak in Ontario, Canada, which led to the loss of measles elimination status. The outbreak, spanning 49 weeks, involved 2377 cases, predominantly among historically under-vaccinated communities. The outbreak strain was identified as a novel N450 sequence and later detected in other countries, including the United States, Mexico, and the Netherlands. The study highlights the fragility of measles elimination in the presence of immunity gaps and emphasizes the need for culturally appropriate community engagement to build trust in immunization and prevent future outbreaks. The findings underscore the importance of surveillance and targeted public health interventions to address vaccine hesitancy and maintain elimination status. The study is descriptive, providing detailed epidemiological data but lacking statistical analyses or causal conclusions, which limits its evidence strength to moderate.

title: Childhood vaccination timeliness, under-immunization-for-age and measles effective immunity in Peru: a province and birth-cohort analysis of national survey data, 2004-2025.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to estimate the timeliness of measles-containing vaccine doses and assess under-immunization-for-age and the gap between effective measles immunity and herd-immunity thresholds in Peru.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The analysis used pooled cross-sections from the 2004-2025 Demographic and Family Health Survey (ENDES) in Peru, focusing on children aged 12-35 months and the 2020-2025 birth cohort across 196 provinces.
analysis.methods: Timeliness was measured in days within WHO age bands for children with visible vaccination cards, and Bayesian small-area models were fitted to estimate the maternal-education gap in DTP3 timeliness.
analysis.main_results: Among children with seen vaccination cards, on-time receipt of DTP3 was 65.3%, while recall-based bounds suggested a range of 54.5%-63.5%. The measles effective immunity proportion was 89.8% in the 2020-2024 birth cohort, below the herd-immunity thresholds for R0 = 15-18.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that card-based estimates may overstate DTP3 timeliness, and measles immunity levels remained below herd-immunity thresholds under the assumed R0 of 15-18.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results highlight the need for improved vaccination timeliness and surveillance to ensure measles immunity reaches herd-immunity thresholds, particularly in provinces with lower immunization rates.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Recall-based bounds introduce uncertainty in DTP3 timeliness estimates, and the study's reliance on survey data may limit generalizability, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed national survey data from Peru (2004-2025) to assess measles vaccination timeliness, under-immunization-for-age, and effective immunity levels. It found that on-time receipt of DTP3 was 65.3% among children with seen vaccination cards, while recall-based bounds suggested a lower range of 54.5%-63.5%. The measles effective immunity proportion was 89.8% in the 2020-2024 birth cohort, below herd-immunity thresholds for R0 = 15-18. The authors concluded that card-based estimates likely overstate timeliness and that measles immunity remains insufficient in many provinces. The study used Bayesian small-area models to estimate the maternal-education gap in DTP3 timeliness, but recall-based bounds and reliance on survey data introduce uncertainty, limiting the confidence in findings.

title: Determinants of Measles Vaccine Failure and Breakthrough Infections: A Systematic Review of IgG Avidity Based Immunological Markers and Host Genetic Polymorphisms.

analysis.scope_and_question: Measles virus remains a leading cause of vaccine-preventable mortality, despite high reported coverage. The review aims to identify determinants of measles vaccine failure and breakthrough infections, focusing on IgG avidity markers and host genetic polymorphisms.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Five databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library) were searched from inception. Studies in vaccinated individuals evaluating IgG avidity markers or host genetic polymorphisms were included. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale, JBI checklist, and modified HuGENet framework. Findings were synthesized narratively (PROSPERO: CRD420261415732).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Sixteen studies (8169 participants; 1998–2025) met inclusion criteria. Across seven studies with event-level data, primary vaccine failure ranged from 24.2% to 90.8%. Reproducible host genetic associations were observed for HLA Class I/II alleles, measles receptor genes (SLAM/CD150, CD46, CD209), TLR pathway genes, antiviral effector genes, and cytokine/cytokine receptor genes. No study reported extractable breakthrough infection or dichotomous IgG avidity data. Reproducible host genetic determinants of measles antibody response cluster at HLA loci, the measles receptor axis, and the TLR pathway.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Inconsistent definitions and absent standardized reporting preclude firm conclusions. Prospective harmonized studies are required.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Replication of findings in larger, more diverse populations is needed. Standardized reporting and definitions are essential for future research. Harmonized prospective studies are required to better understand the determinants of measles vaccine failure and breakthrough infections.

analysis.summary_en: This review identified determinants of measles vaccine failure and breakthrough infections, focusing on IgG avidity markers and host genetic polymorphisms. Sixteen studies met inclusion criteria, with primary vaccine failure ranging from 24.2% to 90.8%. Reproducible host genetic associations were observed, but standardized reporting is needed for future research.

title: Spatio-temporal dynamics, transmission hotspots, and vaccination gaps driving measles persistence in Nigeria, 2006-2025.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Measles remains a major public health concern in Nigeria, contributing disproportionately to the global burden.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study conducted a national retrospective ecological analysis integrating 19 years of surveillance data (2006-2025) and geospatial information, with a focused 4-year analysis of vaccination records (2021-2024).
analysis.methods: Analytical methods included time-series decomposition, spatial autocorrelation (Local Moran's I and Getis-Ord Gi*), and linear mixed-effects modeling to quantify vaccination effects while accounting for state-level heterogeneity.
analysis.main_results: Analysis of 253,595 measles cases revealed a highly clustered geographic distribution, with 86.4% of the national burden concentrated in northern Nigeria. We identified 38 persistent hotspot Local Government Areas that accounted for 23.2% of all cases. Mixed-effects modeling confirmed a significant negative association between MCV1 coverage and the measles case ratio, while MCV2 coverage did not show a statistically significant independent effect.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the role of entrenched hotspots in the north and critical vaccination gaps in the south as key drivers of measles transmission, offering a novel perspective on the spatio-temporal dynamics of the disease.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform targeted public health interventions, emphasizing the need for intensive supplemental immunization activities and routine immunization strengthening in specific regions to address measles persistence.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its ecological design, which may obscure individual-level factors, and the reliance on aggregated surveillance data, which could introduce bias. The evidence strength is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the spatio-temporal dynamics and vaccination gaps driving measles persistence in Nigeria from 2006 to 2025. It reveals that 86.4% of measles cases are concentrated in northern Nigeria, with 38 persistent hotspots accounting for 23.2% of all cases. The analysis shows a significant negative association between MCV1 coverage and measles case ratios, while MCV2 coverage lacks a statistically significant effect. The study underscores the need for tailored strategies to address endemic transmission in the north and close routine immunization gaps in the south. However, the ecological design and reliance on aggregated data limit the confidence in the findings, resulting in a moderate evidence strength.

title: Acute measles encephalitis in adults: a case series in Vietnam.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Acute measles encephalitis is a rare but severe complication of measles, particularly in adults, and carries high mortality and a substantial risk of neurological sequelae. Most descriptions come from children, and the presentation, pathogenesis, and management of adult disease remain poorly defined.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We describe four adults (aged 34-45 years) admitted with fever, rash, and altered mental status. The study is a case series conducted in Vietnam.
analysis.methods: Acute measles infection was confirmed by serum measles-specific IgM or measles virus RNA on real-time reverse-transcription PCR. Cerebrospinal fluid pleocytosis ranged from 57 to 1046 cells/μL, and improved in most patients within 3 days of intravenous immunoglobulin.
analysis.main_results: Measles virus RNA was detected in cerebrospinal fluid in Case 1, indicating primary measles encephalitis. Case 4 showed progressive thalamic and temporal lesions on magnetic resonance imaging. Two patients recovered without neurological sequelae, one survived with residual deficits, and one died from persistent cerebral injury complicated by multidrug-resistant septic shock.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In adults, acute measles encephalitis may reflect a biphasic process that combines direct viral neuroinvasion with immune-mediated inflammation, rather than a purely postinfectious phenomenon.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the potential for measles virus to cause severe neurological complications in adults, emphasizing the need for improved surveillance and management strategies for this population.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its case series design, which cannot establish the therapeutic role of intravenous immunoglobulin. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a case series of four adults with acute measles encephalitis in Vietnam, highlighting the severity and neurological complications associated with the disease in adults. The cases demonstrate varied presentations, including primary measles encephalitis and immune-mediated inflammation, with some patients recovering and others experiencing fatal outcomes. The findings underscore the need for better understanding and management of measles encephalitis in adults, as most descriptions of the condition come from pediatric cases. The study's limitations include its observational design, which prevents definitive conclusions about treatment efficacy. The evidence is moderate, as the results are based on clinical observations rather than controlled trials.

title: Spatiotemporal distribution of timely measles-containing vaccine coverage among children born in Hebei Province during 2019-2023: a secondary analysis of provincial routine immunisation registry data.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to analyse the spatiotemporal distribution characteristics of timely measles-containing vaccine (MCV1) coverage among children born in Hebei Province, China, from 2019 to 2023, to address the scientific and public-health problem of suboptimal vaccination rates and the knowledge gap regarding regional and temporal variations in coverage.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a population-based cross-sectional secondary data analysis of routine provincial immunisation registry data from all county-level districts in Hebei Province, China, involving a total birth cohort of 2,831,956 children born between 1 January 2019 and 31 December 2023 who remained in the province until 8 months of age.
analysis.methods: The study used routine provincial immunisation registry data for secondary analysis, including primary outcome measures of timely MCV1 vaccination coverage and secondary outcomes of global spatial autocorrelation, local spatial clustering and spatiotemporal distribution characteristics.
analysis.main_results: The overall timely coverage of MCV1 among children born in Hebei Province from 2019 to 2023 was 43.49%, showing an increasing trend from 40.57% in 2019 to 53.35% in 2023 (Cochran-Armitage trend test χ2=16 059.55, p<0.05). Pronounced seasonal variations were observed, with lower coverage among children born in the second quarter, followed by a gradual increase in the third quarter.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings revealed significant positive global spatial autocorrelation at the county level, with high-high clusters primarily in central-southern and northeastern Hebei Province, while low-low clusters were mainly concentrated in the northwestern region.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that targeted, season-specific interventions in identified low-coverage clusters may improve timeliness of measles-containing vaccine (MCV1) administration, offering specific implications for surveillance and public health strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on registry data, which may have inherent biases or missing information, and the evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the analysis and potential confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a secondary analysis of routine immunisation registry data from Hebei Province, China, to examine the spatiotemporal distribution of timely measles-containing vaccine (MCV1) coverage among children born between 2019 and 2023. The overall coverage was 43.49%, with an increasing trend over the study period. Seasonal variations were noted, with lower coverage in the second quarter and higher in the third. Spatial clustering showed high-high and low-low clusters in different regions of the province. The authors concluded that targeted interventions in low-coverage areas could improve vaccine timeliness. The study's findings highlight the need for season-specific strategies and further research into individual-level barriers to vaccination. The evidence is moderate due to the observational design and potential biases in registry data.

title: Estimating the incidence and duration of diagnostic delays for measles.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Although measles was declared eliminated in the United States in 2000, cases have increased in recent years. The study aimed to address the issue of diagnostic delays for measles.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed a case-crossover design using the Merative MarketScan Research Databases from 2001 to 2023. It identified measles cases and evaluated prior healthcare encounters for potential missed diagnostic opportunities.
analysis.methods: A bootstrapping approach was used to estimate the number of healthcare visits representing possible missed opportunities to diagnose measles during a two-week period preceding the index diagnosis. Firth logistic regression was utilized to assess factors associated with delays.
analysis.main_results: The study identified 4,651 measles cases. During the two-week period prior to diagnosis, 426 (9.2%) patients had healthcare visits with signs or symptoms commonly associated with measles. It estimated 381 (95%CI: 330-440) missed opportunities to diagnose measles. Delays occurred most frequently in outpatient settings (81.0%). Approximately 6.9% (95%CI: 6.1-8.0%) of patients experienced at least one missed opportunity, with a mean delay of 4.05 days (95%CI: 3.48-4.51) (median delay = 2.94 days [95%CI: 2.00-3.00]). An estimated 1.7% (95%CI: 1.1-2.2%) of patients experienced a diagnostic delay lasting a week or longer.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that diagnostic delays for measles are not uncommon and may facilitate transmission, especially in outpatient settings. This study provides novel insights into the frequency and factors associated with diagnostic delays for measles.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health strategies to improve measles diagnosis and reduce transmission, particularly in outpatient settings. They highlight the importance of identifying factors contributing to diagnostic delays to enhance surveillance and clinical practices.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on healthcare encounter data and potential biases in case identification. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on a case-crossover design and statistical modeling.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to estimate the incidence and duration of diagnostic delays for measles in the United States. Using a case-crossover design with the Merative MarketScan Research Databases from 2001 to 2023, the researchers identified 4,651 measles cases and evaluated prior healthcare encounters for missed diagnostic opportunities. They found that 426 (9.2%) patients had visits with measles-associated symptoms, and 381 (95%CI: 330-440) missed opportunities were estimated. Delays were most common in outpatient settings, with a mean delay of 4.05 days. Factors like age <2 years and antibiotic prescriptions were linked to increased delays. The authors concluded that diagnostic delays are not uncommon and may contribute to measles transmission. The study provides insights into the factors influencing diagnostic delays but is limited by its reliance on healthcare data and potential biases.

title: Predictors of severe measles outcomes in hospitalized patients in Jerusalem, 2025.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Measles is a vaccine-preventable disease. Defining risk factors for poor outcomes in hospitalized patients can improve future measles outbreak preparedness.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Data were collected on all confirmed measles cases that were evaluated at one of the emergency departments (ED) in the three main hospitals in Jerusalem from the first reported case of the current outbreak on April 10th to December 31st, 2025. Complete data were available for 567 patients, of whom 303 (53.4%) were males. Most patients were unvaccinated (91.0%).
analysis.methods: Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were analyzed using robust Poisson multivariable models to calculate incidence rate ratios (IRR) for hospitalization, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) and death.
analysis.main_results: Among 786 individuals who visited the ED with confirmed measles, the rates of hospital admission (≥1 day), ICU, ECMO and death were 83.4%, 6.4%, 0.8%, and 1.4%, respectively. Median age was 2.1 years (IQR 1.2-3.8), and 474 (83.6%) were younger than 5 years. Secondary infections were frequent, including lobar pneumonia (28.7%) and community-acquired bacteremia (3.5%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Respiratory compromise, severe dehydration, and bacteremia identified patients at increased risk of severe outcomes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Respiratory support and severe dehydration were associated with hospital admission and ICU admission, and community-acquired bacteremia was associated with death or ECMO. These findings can inform targeted surveillance and intervention strategies for measles outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations. The study provides high confidence in identifying predictors of severe measles outcomes based on robust statistical analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to define risk factors for poor outcomes in hospitalized measles patients in Jerusalem, 2025. It analyzed data from confirmed measles cases evaluated at three main hospitals between April 10th and December 31st, 2025. The main results showed that 83.4% of patients were hospitalized, 6.4% required ICU admission, 0.8% needed ECMO, and 1.4% died. Respiratory compromise, severe dehydration, and community-acquired bacteremia were associated with severe outcomes. The findings highlight the importance of identifying risk factors for severe measles outcomes to improve outbreak preparedness and inform targeted interventions. The study used robust statistical methods, providing moderate confidence in its results.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the growing susceptibility to infectious diseases, with a focus on measles virus, as Canada’s loss of measles elimination status serves as a warning.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is an editorial that reflects on the implications of Canada’s loss of measles elimination status, highlighting the broader public health concern.
analysis.methods: The editorial does not describe specific methods or procedures but discusses the context and implications of measles resurgence.
analysis.main_results: The editorial reports that Canada has lost its measles elimination status, indicating a rise in measles cases and susceptibility.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the loss of measles elimination status as a sign of increasing vulnerability to infectious diseases, emphasizing the need for renewed public health efforts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the importance of maintaining measles control measures and highlight the risks of complacency in public health strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations, but the editorial is based on observed public health trends and is considered to have moderate confidence.

analysis.summary_en: This editorial discusses the implications of Canada’s loss of measles elimination status, highlighting the growing susceptibility to infectious diseases. The authors emphasize the need for renewed public health efforts to combat measles resurgence. The study is based on observed trends and does not include detailed methods or statistical analyses. The findings suggest that maintaining measles control measures is critical for public health. The editorial serves as a call to action rather than a data-driven analysis. The evidence is considered to have moderate confidence due to the lack of specific limitations reported.

title: Post‐Measles Complications and Mortality in Children under Five Years in Low‐ and Middle‐Income Countries: A Narrative Review

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the measles virus, measles disease, and its complications in children under five years in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). The central question is to examine the epidemiological evidence on post-measles complications (PMCs), their pathogenesis, and the need for integrated post-measles care strategies in vulnerable populations.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This narrative review included all papers that published primary data on any of the PMCs in the last 55 years, identified through PubMed and Google Scholar. The review does not report a meta-analysis or pooled estimate but synthesizes existing literature to address the research question.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Epidemiological data show that 30–40% of measles cases in LMICs develop complications, including pneumonia, diarrhea, otitis media, and, less commonly, encephalitis and ocular disease. PMCs are frequently misattributed to independent illnesses because they often emerge after a delay following the acute infection. Measles-induced immune amnesia renders affected individuals vulnerable to secondary infections for up to 2–3 years post-infection. In LMICs and conflict-affected settings, this prolonged immunological vulnerability intersects with pre-existing risk factors such as malnutrition, micronutrient deficiencies, and poor healthcare access, which amplify the consequences substantially.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights that PMCs are frequently misattributed to independent illnesses due to their delayed onset. Additionally, the review notes that measles elimination remains challenging in resource-limited and conflict-affected contexts, which may contribute to the persistence of PMCs. The evidence does not report specific data on the relative frequency or severity of PMCs across different measles virus genotypes or regions, indicating a gap in understanding the geographic and genetic variability of PMCs.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Integrated post-measles care strategies are urgently needed from a global health perspective, especially in resource-limited and conflict-affected settings. The review emphasizes the importance of addressing the prolonged immunological vulnerability caused by measles-induced immune amnesia and the need for improved surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment of PMCs in vulnerable populations.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review examines the epidemiological evidence on post-measles complications (PMCs) in children under five years in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). It highlights that PMCs, including pneumonia, diarrhea, and otitis media, are a significant consequence of measles infection, often misattributed to other illnesses due to their delayed onset. Measles-induced immune amnesia increases susceptibility to secondary infections for up to 2–3 years post-infection, which is exacerbated by pre-existing risk factors such as malnutrition and poor healthcare access in LMICs. The review underscores the need for integrated post-measles care strategies, especially in resource-limited and conflict-affected settings, as measles cases resurge globally. The evidence does not provide detailed data on the geographic or genetic variability of PMCs, indicating a need for further research.

title: Characterizing the relative strength of metapopulation dynamics in measles persistence

analysis.research_question_and_background: Measles remains persistent globally despite vaccination efforts, highlighting the need to understand the mechanisms driving its persistence.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study uses a metapopulation compartmental model and historical/subnational incidence data from the USA and Nigeria to analyze measles persistence.
analysis.methods: The researchers developed a novel scale-free measure called roundness, which quantifies the contribution of metapopulation dynamics to measles persistence using simulations and observed data.
analysis.main_results: In the USA, roundness nearly doubled after the introduction of the measles-containing vaccine, and in Nigeria, it is well correlated with vaccine coverage, distinguishing between local and regional persistence.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that metapopulation dynamics significantly influence measles persistence, even when local prevalence is reduced by vaccination, offering a new way to assess persistence mechanisms.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This measure can inform control strategies by identifying whether persistence is due to local factors or regional connectivity, particularly in areas lacking detailed surveillance data.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on historical and subnational data, which may have limitations in capturing real-time dynamics, but the evidence is supported by both simulations and observed data, giving it a moderate confidence level.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the relative role of local and regional dynamics in measles persistence. Using a metapopulation model and incidence data from the USA and Nigeria, the researchers developed a novel measure called roundness to quantify the contribution of metapopulation dynamics. They found that roundness increased in the USA after vaccination and correlated with vaccine coverage in Nigeria, indicating that persistence can be driven by different mechanisms. The study highlights the importance of understanding these dynamics for effective control strategies, especially in areas with limited surveillance. However, the reliance on historical data introduces limitations, and the evidence is considered moderate in strength.

title: Is the Pennsylvania Measles Outbreak the New Normal?

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate whether the Pennsylvania measles outbreak represents a new normal due to declining vaccine coverage.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is an observational analysis of measles outbreaks in Pennsylvania and other US states, focusing on trends in vaccine coverage and outbreak patterns.
analysis.methods: The study utilized public health data and surveillance reports to assess measles outbreak trends and vaccine coverage rates across multiple states.
analysis.main_results: The article reports that measles outbreaks in Pennsylvania and other US states have increased in frequency and scale, coinciding with declining vaccine coverage rates.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as indicative of a potential shift in measles epidemiology, suggesting that the outbreaks may become more common unless vaccination rates improve.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of maintaining high vaccination rates to prevent the resurgence of measles and inform public health strategies for outbreak control.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on observational data and does not include detailed statistical analysis, which limits the strength of the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This article examines the ongoing measles outbreaks in Pennsylvania and other US states, suggesting that they may represent a new normal due to declining vaccine coverage. The study is observational, relying on public health data to assess trends in outbreak frequency and vaccine rates. It reports an increase in measles outbreaks alongside lower vaccination rates, interpreting this as a potential shift in epidemiology. The findings emphasize the need for sustained vaccination efforts to prevent further outbreaks. However, the study lacks detailed statistical analysis, which limits the strength of its conclusions. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on available surveillance data without experimental validation.

title: What the West Texas Measles Outbreak Taught Me About Public Health Leadership

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to examine the lessons learned from the West Texas measles outbreak regarding public health leadership and response strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a commentary on the West Texas measles outbreak, which occurred in 2026, and focuses on public health leadership and management practices during the event.
analysis.methods: The methods involved a retrospective analysis of public health leadership strategies and outcomes during the West Texas measles outbreak, including case management, communication protocols, and community engagement.
analysis.main_results: The commentary highlights the importance of coordinated leadership, rapid response, and community engagement in mitigating the spread of measles during the outbreak.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the outbreak as a case study demonstrating the critical role of effective public health leadership in managing infectious disease outbreaks, offering novel insights into leadership practices.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health leadership training and preparedness for future outbreaks, emphasizing the need for proactive and collaborative strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a commentary and does not include quantitative data, which limits the strength of the evidence but provides valuable qualitative insights.

analysis.summary_en: This commentary reflects on the West Texas measles outbreak of 2026, emphasizing the importance of public health leadership in managing infectious disease crises. The study outlines the challenges faced during the outbreak and highlights the need for coordinated, rapid, and community-focused responses. While the analysis is qualitative and lacks quantitative data, it offers novel insights into leadership practices that can inform future outbreak management. The findings suggest that effective leadership is crucial for controlling measles outbreaks and improving public health preparedness. The study's limitations include its reliance on a narrative rather than empirical data, which affects the strength of the evidence but does not diminish its value as a case study.

title: Timeliness of Measles Outbreak Detection, Notification, and Response in Uganda: A 7-1-7 Target Assessment, January–December 2025

analysis.research_question_and_background: Measles is among the most transmissible human infections, and delays in outbreak detection and response can rapidly amplify community transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The 7-1-7 target provides an operational benchmark for evaluating outbreak detection, notification, and early response. We assessed 46 laboratory-confirmed measles outbreaks reported in Uganda during 2025 with complete 7-1-7 data.
analysis.methods: Detection (T1) was measured from outbreak emergence to first recording by the surveillance system, notification (T2) from detection to notification of public health authorities, and response (T3) from notification to achievement of the final applicable early response milestone. Timeliness was summarised using medians, IQRs, and proportions meeting each target; new and recurrent outbreaks were compared using Fisher’s exact tests with exact 95% CIs.
analysis.main_results: Among 46 outbreaks, the median detection interval was 16 days (IQR: 8–31), notification interval 1 day (IQR: 0–5), and response interval 34 days (IQR: 22–49). Eight outbreaks (17.4%) met the 7-day detection target, 27 (58.7%) met the 1-day notification target, and two (4.3%) achieved all seven early response milestones within 7 days of notification; none met all three 7-1-7 targets.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Measles outbreaks in Uganda were generally detected late and responded to slowly, despite comparatively timely notification.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Improving performance will require stronger community- and facility-based surveillance, timely laboratory confirmation, functional district coordination structures, and reliable access to vaccines, transport, cold-chain capacity, and operational funding.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations of the study design.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the timeliness of measles outbreak detection, notification, and response in Uganda during 2025 using the 7-1-7 framework. It finds that while notification was relatively timely, detection and response were delayed. The median detection interval was 16 days, notification interval 1 day, and response interval 34 days. Only 17.4% of outbreaks met the 7-day detection target, 58.7% met the 1-day notification target, and 4.3% achieved all seven early response milestones within 7 days of notification. None met all three 7-1-7 targets. The study highlights the need for improved community- and facility-based surveillance, timely laboratory confirmation, functional district coordination, and reliable access to vaccines and operational funds. The findings suggest that while notification was efficient, delays in detection and response were linked to low clinical suspicion, limited community-based surveillance, and shortages of resources.

title: Burden and clinical characteristics of measles in pre-vaccination age infants

analysis.research_question_and_background: Measles remains an important cause of childhood morbidity, particularly among infants who are below the routine age for measles-rubella vaccination. These infants may be vulnerable because of declining maternal antibodies and absence of vaccine-derived protection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study assessed the burden and clinical characteristics of measles among hospitalized children, with particular attention to the pre-vaccination-age group. A total of 300 children aged 1 month to 12 years admitted to the measles isolation ward were included.
analysis.methods: This hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted in the Department of Pediatrics, Mugda Medical College Hospital, Dhaka, from March 2026 to May 2026. Data on demographic characteristics, age, clinical manifestations, complications, management and outcomes were collected using a structured proforma. Measles was diagnosed according to the WHO clinical case definition.
analysis.main_results: Males constituted 61.7% of participants, while 38.3% were female. Infants younger than 1 year represented 57.1% of cases, including 102 (34.0%) infants below 9 months. Fever and rash were present in all patients. Cough, coryza and conjunctivitis were reported in 82.7%, 78.9% and 73.7%, respectively. Pneumonia was the most frequent complication, affecting 63.9% of patients, followed by diarrhea (45.1%) and vomiting (30.1%). All patients received supportive care, while 18.8% required oxygen therapy. ICU admission was required in 0.72% and mortality was 1.0%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Measles caused substantial morbidity among hospitalized children, with pre-vaccination-age infants comprising a considerable proportion of cases. Early recognition, prompt supportive management and strengthened preventive strategies are essential to reduce severe measles-related outcomes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for targeted surveillance and prevention strategies in pre-vaccination-age infants to mitigate the burden of measles. Strengthened preventive measures could help reduce severe outcomes in this vulnerable group.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in a single hospital, which may limit generalisability. The evidence is based on clinical case definitions and is therefore limited in specificity, but the high sample size and clear reporting of outcomes provide moderate confidence in the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the burden and clinical characteristics of measles among hospitalized children, with a focus on pre-vaccination-age infants. Conducted in a single hospital in Dhaka, it collected data on demographics, symptoms, complications, and outcomes using a structured proforma and WHO clinical case definitions. Results show that measles caused substantial morbidity, with infants under 1 year representing 57.1% of cases. Fever and rash were universal, while pneumonia was the most frequent complication. All patients received supportive care, with 18.8% needing oxygen therapy and 0.72% requiring ICU admission, resulting in a 1.0% mortality rate. The authors emphasize the importance of early recognition and strengthened preventive strategies to reduce severe outcomes. The study's single-center design and reliance on clinical case definitions limit generalizability, but the moderate confidence in findings is supported by the comprehensive data collection and clear reporting of outcomes.

title: SVIR Model Analysis of Measles with Incomplete Vaccination and 1 Waning Immunity: Sidoarjo-Indonesia Case

analysis.research_question_and_background: The basicreproduction number R0 is derived using the next-generation matrix method, and the globalstability of both the disease-free and endemic equilibria is rigorously proven via Lyapunovfunctions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The supplied evidence does not clearly state the study design, setting, or study population.
analysis.methods: This study develops andanalyzes a Susceptible–Vaccinated–Infected–Recovered (SVIR) compartmental model formeasles transmission in Sidoarjo City, Indonesia, incorporating waning immunity.
analysis.main_results: Model parameters are estimated from weekly 2023 surveillance data in Sidoarjo Cityusing Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Extended Kalman Filter, Maximum LikelihoodEstimation, and Least Squares, and evaluated via Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE).PSO achieves the lowest MAPE (11.17%), outperforming the other methods.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The estimatedR0 = 0.668confirms a disease-free regime.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Measles remains a significant public health challenge in Indonesia, especially in regionswith heterogeneous vaccination coverage and waning immunity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Normalized sensitivity analysis identifies vaccineefficacy as the most influential parameter; a decline in efficacy to0 .75elevates R0 close tothe critical threshold, and any further reduction pushes the system into an endemic state.These findings underscore the necessity of maintaining high vaccine efficacy through boosterprograms and strengthened immunization strategies to sustain measles elimination at thedistrict level.

analysis.summary_en: The basicreproduction number R0 is derived using the next-generation matrix method, and the globalstability of both the disease-free and endemic equilibria is rigorously proven via Lyapunovfunctions. The supplied evidence does not clearly state the study design, setting, or study population. This study develops andanalyzes a Susceptible–Vaccinated–Infected–Recovered (SVIR) compartmental model formeasles transmission in Sidoarjo City, Indonesia, incorporating waning immunity. Model parameters are estimated from weekly 2023 surveillance data in Sidoarjo Cityusing Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Extended Kalman Filter, Maximum LikelihoodEstimation, and Least Squares, and evaluated via Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE).PSO achieves the lowest MAPE (11.17%), outperforming the other methods. The estimatedR0 = 0.668confirms a disease-free regime. Measles remains a significant public health challenge in Indonesia, especially in regionswith heterogeneous vaccination coverage and waning immunity. Normalized sensitivity analysis identifies vaccineefficacy as the most influential parameter; a decline in efficacy to0 .75elevates R0 close tothe critical threshold, and any further reduction pushes the system into an endemic state.These findings underscore the necessity of maintaining high vaccine efficacy through boosterprograms and strengthened immunization strategies to sustain measles elimination at thedistrict level.

title: Measles-Specific IgG Antibody Levels and Associated Demographic and Vaccination Factors Among Children in Diyala Governorate, Iraq: A Cross-Sectional Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Measles is a significant cause of death in children, despite the availability of safe and cost-effective measles vaccines. This study aimed to assess measles IgG antibody levels and identify associated factors affecting measles immunity among children in Diyala Governorate / Iraq.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted between October 1, 2025, and April 30, 2026. Ninety children aged 1–14 years who had received at least one dose of a measles-containing vaccine were enrolled from primary health care centres in Diyala Governorate.
analysis.methods: Venous blood samples were collected, and serum anti-measles IgG antibody concentrations were determined using the enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Demographic characteristics and vaccination history were obtained through a structured questionnaire.
analysis.main_results: Female children showed significantly higher measles IgG antibody concentrations than males (64.74 ± 58.91 vs. 46.60 ± 46.55 ng/L; P = 0.006). No significant differences in measles IgG antibody concentrations were observed according to vaccination status (65.77 ± 73.29 vs. 50.48 ± 41.64 ng/L; P = 0.682) or age groups (P = 0.341).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights a significant gender difference in measles IgG antibody levels, which may inform targeted public health interventions. A weak positive correlation was found between measles IgG antibody concentration and the number of vaccine doses, though it was not statistically significant.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform measles surveillance and vaccination strategies, particularly in identifying demographic factors that may influence immune response. This could aid in improving vaccine coverage and effectiveness in children.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which cannot establish causality. The evidence is moderate as it is based on a single time point and does not account for long-term immunity or other confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study conducted in Diyala Governorate, Iraq, between October 1, 2025, and April 30, 2026, aimed to assess measles-specific IgG antibody levels and identify associated factors affecting measles immunity among children aged 1–14 years. Blood samples were collected, and serum anti-measles IgG antibody concentrations were measured using ELISA. Demographic data and vaccination history were gathered through questionnaires. The results showed significantly higher measles IgG antibody concentrations in female children compared to males, but no significant differences were observed based on vaccination status or age groups. A weak positive correlation between antibody concentration and the number of vaccine doses was noted, though it was not statistically significant. The study suggests that gender may be a factor influencing measles immunity, which could inform targeted public health interventions. However, the cross-sectional design limits the ability to establish causality, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the lack of long-term data and potential confounding variables.

title: Development of a New Lyophilized Live-Attenuated Measles–Rubella (MR) Vaccine Formulation Designed for Lower-Cost Production in Africa

analysis.research_question_and_background: This work aimed to develop a new, lyophilized, live-attenuated measles–rubella (MR) vaccine formulation designed for lower-cost production in Africa, addressing the need for affordable and stable vaccines in resource-limited settings.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the development of lab-scale and pilot-scale freeze-drying cycles for a lyophilized MR vaccine formulation, with the population consisting of viral bulks produced in MRC-5 cells and evaluated for stability under various conditions.
analysis.methods: Both lab-scale and pilot-scale freeze-drying cycles were developed, a high-throughput RT-qPCR-based viral infectivity assay was implemented, and effective excipient screening conditions were employed to identify stabilizing additives for MR viruses.
analysis.main_results: First, protein-based bulking agents were avoided in favor of sucrose/mannitol mixtures. Second, ~50 excipients were screened, and two additional key stabilizing components were identified: sodium phosphate buffer and urea. Stability assessments were performed on different variations of a candidate lyophilized MR formulation to elucidate the inter-relationships between sucrose–mannitol ratios, cake integrity, and MR virus stability.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results demonstrated the feasibility of a new, lower-cost, lyophilized, multidose MR formulation for potential use with a live-attenuated MR vaccine candidate targeted for local production in Africa.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more affordable and stable MR vaccines for use in Africa, potentially improving immunization programs and disease prevention efforts.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, and the results are based on stability assessments under controlled conditions, which may not fully represent real-world scenarios. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a new, lyophilized, live-attenuated measles–rubella (MR) vaccine formulation designed for lower-cost production in Africa. The formulation was created using non-animal-derived excipients and high-titer MR viral bulks produced in MRC-5 cells. Lab-scale and pilot-scale freeze-drying cycles were developed, and a high-throughput RT-qPCR-based viral infectivity assay was used to evaluate stability. The results showed that sucrose/mannitol mixtures were preferred over protein-based bulking agents, and two key stabilizing components—sodium phosphate buffer and urea—were identified. Stability assessments revealed promising profiles for the optimized formulation under real-time and accelerated storage conditions. The findings suggest the feasibility of a lower-cost, multidose MR vaccine for local production in Africa, which could enhance immunization programs. However, the study is limited to abstract-only evidence, and the results are based on controlled conditions, which may not fully reflect real-world applications. The evidence strength is moderate.

title: Socioeconomic Determinants of Measles Incidence, Outbreaks, and Vaccination Non-Completion Among Children Under Five in Southeast Asia: A Systematic Review

analysis.research_question_and_background: This systematic review investigates the relationship between socioeconomic status (SES) and measles incidence, outbreaks, transmission, and routine immunization non-completion among children under five years of age in Southeast Asia.
analysis.study_design_and_population: By systematically synthesizing empirical quantitative observational studies (cross-sectional, cohort, case-control, and ecological) published in English between 2016 and 2025, this project aims to isolate the primary socioeconomic determinants influencing measles infection and incomplete vaccination within Southeast Asian countries like Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, the Philippines, and Vietnam.
analysis.methods: The study design_population includes cross-sectional, cohort, case-control, and ecological studies published in English between 2016 and 2025, focusing on empirical quantitative observational data.
analysis.main_results: The supplied evidence does not report specific results or statistical findings.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The supplied evidence does not report explicit interpretation or novelty claims.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study aims to provide empirical, context-specific evidence to help public health policymakers design targeted equity interventions, strengthen routine immunization coverage, and prevent measles outbreaks across vulnerable pediatric populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations or evidence strength assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review explores the socioeconomic determinants of measles incidence, outbreaks, and vaccination non-completion among children under five in Southeast Asia. The study synthesizes empirical quantitative observational data from cross-sectional, cohort, case-control, and ecological studies published between 2016 and 2025. The focus is on understanding how context-specific parental factors, such as household income, parental education, maternal literacy, and employment status, interact with structural healthcare access to influence pediatric disease susceptibility. The findings aim to inform targeted public health interventions to improve immunization coverage and prevent outbreaks. However, the evidence provided does not include specific results, interpretations, or limitations, which are necessary for a comprehensive evaluation of the study's validity and impact.

title: Factors Associated with Length of Hospital Stay and Clinical Characteristics of Children Hospitalized with Measles

analysis.research_question_and_background: To evaluate the clinical characteristics, complications, and factors associated with the length of hospital stay in children hospitalized with measles.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective, observational study included children aged 0-18 years hospitalized with measles between January and December 2023 at a tertiary care center in Istanbul, Türkiye.
analysis.methods: Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and hospitalization data were analyzed.
analysis.main_results: Sixty-one hospitalized children with measles were included; 52.5% were younger than 5 years, 47.5% were older than 5 years, 59% were Turkish citizens, 41% were foreign nationals, 57.4% were male, and 77% were unvaccinated. Fever and rash were present in all patients. Pneumonia was the most common complication (68.9%), followed by hepatitis (11.5%), gingivostomatitis (11.5%), ocular complications (9.8%), and otitis (4.9%). All hepatitis cases occurred in children older than 5 years. Three patients (5.2%) required pediatric intensive care.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In univariable linear regression analyses, pneumonia/bronchopneumonia, C-reactive protein (CRP), and white blood cell count were significantly associated with longer hospital stay. In the primary multivariable linear regression model, only CRP remained independently associated with prolonged hospitalization (B = 0.017, 95% CI = 0.0002-0.0333; P = .047). Inflammatory markers were associated with prolonged hospitalization, suggesting that systemic inflammation may contribute to longer inpatient care.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Measles remains a major public health problem, particularly among unvaccinated children. Larger multicenter studies are needed to confirm these findings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and the need for larger multicenter studies to confirm these findings. The sample size is relatively small, and the study was conducted at a single center, which may limit generalizability.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated clinical characteristics and factors associated with hospital stay in children with measles. Of 61 patients, 77% were unvaccinated, and pneumonia was the most common complication. CRP levels were the only independent predictor of prolonged hospitalization, suggesting systemic inflammation contributes to longer inpatient care.

title: Estimating measles vaccine effectiveness from Japanese public surveillance data with quantitative bias analysis: study protocol and statistical analysis plan (version 2.4)

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aims to estimate measles vaccine effectiveness (VE) in Japan using public surveillance data, addressing the challenge of accurately assessing VE in an elimination setting where case numbers are small and reference populations may not align with case-generating populations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a protocol for estimating VE using Japanese public surveillance data, focusing on measles cases and vaccination history across three time periods (2008-2014, 2015-2019, 2020-2025), primarily in children aged 2-4 years.
analysis.methods: The study employs a screening method to estimate VE from published Japanese aggregate data, comparing one or more doses of measles vaccine against none, using a two-group binomial likelihood model with calendar year adjustments and 95 percent profile-likelihood intervals.
analysis.main_results: The main results include VE estimates for children aged 2-4 years, with secondary results reported for ages 5-19 years.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as highlighting the limitations of conditional inference in VE estimation, emphasizing that a sensitivity range crossing zero does not imply vaccine ineffectiveness but rather reflects methodological constraints.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance strategies and the interpretation of VE in elimination settings, contributing to improved understanding of vaccine performance and potential biases in data collection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges limitations such as missing vaccination data and potential selection mismatch, but the evidence strength is considered moderate due to the use of synthetic data verification and a registered interpretation rule.

analysis.summary_en: This study outlines a protocol for estimating measles vaccine effectiveness (VE) in Japan using public surveillance data. It addresses the challenge of VE estimation in an elimination setting, where small case numbers and mismatch between case-generating populations and reference samples limit accuracy. The methods involve a screening approach using a two-group binomial likelihood model with calendar year adjustments and 95 percent profile-likelihood intervals. The main results include VE estimates for children aged 2-4 years, with secondary results for ages 5-19 years. The authors interpret these findings as demonstrating the limitations of conditional inference, noting that a sensitivity range crossing zero does not indicate vaccine ineffectiveness. The study's implications for public health include informing surveillance strategies and improving the interpretation of VE in elimination contexts. The evidence strength is moderate, as the study accounts for biases through quantitative bias analysis and synthetic data verification, but it does not yet present real-data VE estimates.

title: Laporan Kasus: Campak (Measles) pada Anak

analysis.research_question_and_background: Campak (measles) remains a major public-health problem in children, and this case report was needed to document clinical presentation, diagnosis, and management in a single pediatric patient.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This is a descriptive case-report study of one 3-year-old boy presenting with fever for seven days, cough, rhinorrhea, conjunctivitis, and a maculopapular rash spreading from the retroauricular region to the whole body.
analysis.methods: The report describes clinical observation, physical examination including Koplik spots on buccal mucosa, laboratory findings of leukopenia with relative lymphocytosis, and supportive management with intravenous fluids, antipyretics, antiemetics, and high-dose vitamin A.
analysis.main_results: Physical examination revealed Koplik spots on buccal mucosa; laboratory tests showed leukopenia with relative lymphocytosis; the patient received supportive care and showed clinical improvement during treatment.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret Koplik spots as a pathognomonic sign supporting clinical diagnosis of measles, and they conclude that adequate supportive therapy yields favorable clinical outcomes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Clinical diagnosis based on characteristic signs and Koplik spots can suffice for measles confirmation, and supportive care including high-dose vitamin A contributes to favorable recovery.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: This is an abstract-only report from a single pediatric case, so the evidence is limited to one patient and cannot establish prevalence, causality, or generalizability beyond the described case.

analysis.summary_en: Measles remains a major public-health problem in children, and this case report documents clinical presentation, diagnosis, and management in a single 3-year-old boy with Koplik spots, leukopenia with relative lymphocytosis, and favorable response to supportive care including high-dose vitamin A.

title: Antiviral activity of HSP90 inhibitors against Mumps virus and related paramyxoviruses

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify potential antiviral agents against measles virus and related paramyxoviruses, given the ongoing global outbreaks of mumps virus and the lack of approved antiviral drugs for these pathogens.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved screening approximately 1,000 small-molecule compounds using a recombinant mumps virus expressing green fluorescent protein to identify those that suppress viral replication without cytotoxicity.
analysis.methods: A recombinant mumps virus expressing green fluorescent protein was used to screen compounds, and time-of-addition assays were conducted to determine the stage of viral replication affected by the inhibitors.
analysis.main_results: Six compounds were identified that significantly suppressed viral replication with no detectable cytotoxicity, and their antiviral efficacy extended to other paramyxoviruses such as measles virus, canine distemper virus, and Sendai virus.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that HSP90 inhibitors could serve as host-directed antiviral agents against paramyxoviruses, offering a new approach for treating emerging and re-emerging infections.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide a foundation for further development of HSP90 inhibitors as potential therapeutic options for paramyxovirus infections, including measles.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro findings, and the evidence strength is moderate as it does not include clinical or in vivo validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the antiviral activity of HSP90 inhibitors against mumps virus and related paramyxoviruses. Despite widespread vaccination, mumps virus continues to cause outbreaks globally, and no approved antiviral drugs exist for it or other paramyxoviruses. The researchers screened 1,000 compounds using a recombinant mumps virus expressing green fluorescent protein and identified six HSP90 inhibitors that suppressed viral replication without cytotoxicity. These compounds showed efficacy against other paramyxoviruses, including measles virus, canine distemper virus, and Sendai virus. The results suggest that HSP90 inhibitors could be a promising host-directed antiviral strategy for paramyxoviruses. However, the study is limited to in vitro experiments, and further research is needed to validate these findings in vivo or clinically. The evidence is moderate due to the lack of clinical data.

title: Neuroimaging in subacute sclerosing panencephalitis: unravelling the spectrum of a devastating encephalopathy

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to explore the role of neuroimaging in understanding the progression and staging of subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE), a devastating complication of measles virus infection. The background highlights that SSPE is a long-term consequence of wild-type measles virus infection, marked by progressive cognitive decline, behavioral abnormalities, and eventual autonomic collapse.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a prospective follow-up study focusing on neuroimaging abnormalities in patients diagnosed with subacute sclerosing panencephalitis. It examines the disease's progression across different stages and its impact on brain structures in children and young adults in tropical countries.
analysis.methods: The study employs conventional and advanced neuroimaging techniques, including magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) mapping, proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS), surface-based morphometry (SBM), and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analysis to assess structural and metabolic changes in SSPE patients.
analysis.main_results: In early stages, MRI findings may be normal or show faint subcortical white matter T2/FLAIR hyperintensities. As the disease progresses, asymmetric parieto-occipital white matter lesions and restricted diffusion are observed. In late stages, confluent white matter loss, basal ganglia/brainstem lesions, and diffuse cerebral/cerebellar atrophy are noted. Advanced imaging techniques reveal decreased N-acetyl aspartate (NAA)/Creatine (Cr) ratio and elevated Choline (Cho)/Creatine (Cr) ratio, indicating neuronal loss and active demyelination.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that neuroimaging has evolved into a critical tool for evaluating disease stage, progression, and atypical variants of SSPE, providing insights into the pathological evolution that are not easily discernible through clinical symptoms alone.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the use of neuroimaging in the staging and differential diagnosis of SSPE, aiding in early detection and guiding clinical management in tropical regions where the disease is prevalent.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on neuroimaging findings without detailed statistical analysis or comparison with other diagnostic methods. The evidence is moderate, as it provides descriptive insights into imaging patterns but lacks broader validation or control groups.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of neuroimaging in understanding the progression of subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE), a severe complication of measles virus infection. It outlines the evolving spectrum of MRI findings across disease stages, from early normal or faint hyperintensities to late-stage atrophy and gliosis. Advanced imaging techniques such as diffusion-weighted imaging and proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy reveal metabolic and structural changes, including decreased N-acetyl aspartate/creatine ratio and elevated choline/creatine ratio, indicating neuronal loss and active demyelination. The authors emphasize that neuroimaging has become a nuanced tool for evaluating disease stage and progression, offering critical insights into the pathological evolution of SSPE. The study's implications highlight the importance of neuroimaging in the differential diagnosis of SSPE, particularly in tropical regions. However, the evidence is moderate due to the lack of detailed statistical analysis and comparison with other diagnostic methods.

title: Germicidal ultraviolet to reduce transmission of respiratory infections indoors: a systematic review.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory infections that transmit through air contribute substantially to global morbidity and mortality. This study aimed to review the effectiveness and safety of germicidal ultraviolet (GUV) for preventing respiratory infection transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study included 57 reports describing 40 studies published between 1940 and 2025, comprising 30 non-randomized controlled trials, 4 randomized controlled trials (RCTs), 4 case series, 1 cohort study, and 1 cross-sectional study.
analysis.methods: DATA SOURCES: Medline, Embase, Global Health, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, Engineering Village, Epistemonikos, Scopus, and Environmental Science Collection were used. STUDY SELECTION: Studies of GUV with a comparator, measuring human outcomes including respiratory infections, absenteeism, or adverse events. DATA EXTRACTION: At least two investigators extracted data.
analysis.main_results: Non-randomized studies indicated GUV reduces infections with high transmissibility through air (measles and chickenpox), although results were mixed for undifferentiated respiratory illnesses and absenteeism. Two RCTs were inconclusive or showed only modest effects. Safety monitoring in 16 studies identified no increased eye or skin irritation from properly installed GUV.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Several older clinical studies indicated that GUV reduces infections with high transmissibility through air, but its broader effectiveness against respiratory infection remains uncertain. Inconclusive results may reflect methodological and epidemiological limitations rather than true ineffectiveness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that GUV may be a useful tool for reducing the transmission of highly transmissible respiratory infections like measles, but further research is needed to confirm its effectiveness against a broader range of respiratory pathogens.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: All studies had at least one threat to validity; 89% were non-randomized, and 83% lacked statistical power calculations. Heterogeneous study designs, interventions, and outcomes precluded meta-analysis. The evidence strength is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review evaluates the effectiveness and safety of germicidal ultraviolet (GUV) for preventing respiratory infection transmission. The study identified 57 reports describing 40 studies published between 1940 and 2025, including non-randomized controlled trials, randomized controlled trials (RCTs), case series, cohort studies, and cross-sectional studies. Non-randomized studies suggested GUV may reduce infections with high transmissibility through air, such as measles and chickenpox, but results were mixed for other respiratory illnesses. Two RCTs were inconclusive or showed only modest effects. Safety monitoring found no increased eye or skin irritation from properly installed GUV. The authors concluded that while older studies indicated GUV's potential for reducing highly transmissible infections, its broader effectiveness remains uncertain. They emphasized the need for adequately powered RCTs with robust clinical endpoints. The study's limitations include heterogeneous designs, lack of statistical power calculations in most studies, and the inability to perform meta-analysis due to variability in interventions and outcomes. The evidence strength is moderate, as the findings are based on a mix of study types with methodological limitations.

title: Multiple Sclerosis and Viruses: « Liaisons Dangereuses ».

analysis.scope_and_question: The review explores the potential role of viral interactions in the etiology of multiple sclerosis (MS), with a focus on the measles virus as a target entity. The central question is whether the interplay among different neurotropic viruses contributes to MS susceptibility, particularly in genetically predisposed individuals.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a comprehensive analysis of the literature on viral interactions and MS. It includes epidemiological, immunological, and experimental data, and evaluates the collective causative role of viral co-exposures. The review does not explicitly report on meta-analysis or consensus processes, but it synthesizes findings from various studies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that viral co-exposures may act synergistically to shape MS susceptibility in genetically predisposed individuals. It highlights the importance of understanding the cumulative and interactive effects of these pathogens in the context of MS development.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review acknowledges contradictory evidence regarding the role of different viral agents in MS. It notes that the molecular mechanisms linking viral infections to MS are not fully understood, and the literature lacks sufficient research on the collective causative role of viral interplay.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that characterising viral interactions presents a new research direction for identifying novel biomarkers and developing preventative strategies through targeted control of viral networks.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the potential role of measles virus and other neurotropic viruses in the etiology of multiple sclerosis (MS). It highlights the growing interest in viral infections as environmental triggers for MS, particularly the synergistic effects of viral co-exposures in genetically predisposed individuals. The review synthesises epidemiological, immunological, and experimental data, noting that while the link between Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and MS is well-established, the involvement of multiple viruses remains under-researched. It identifies key controversies and evidence gaps, such as the lack of clarity on molecular mechanisms and the need for more studies on viral interactions. The review proposes that understanding these interactions could lead to new research directions, including the development of preventative strategies targeting viral networks.
